claim: Researchers can add and revise shared scenario turns without a model while retaining exact-parent attribution, immutable lineage, visible stale-draft recovery, and deterministic concurrent sibling convergence.
commands: npm --prefix frontend run test -- src/workspace/ScenarioTurnWorkspace.ui.test.tsx src/workspace/ScenarioWorkspace.ui.test.ts src/workspace/scenarioModel.test.ts src/workspace/scenarioAutomation.test.ts src/workspace/scenarioPack.test.ts --reporter=verbose
proved: The selected-scenario product surface exposes manual Add turn and Edit actions that perform no model or network call.
Creating a turn stores its role, content, installation researcher ID, timestamp, and stable turn/revision identities.
Editing appends one immutable exact-parent attributed revision and retains every earlier revision in lineage.
The domain refuses a stale expected-current revision before mutation while preserving exact-retry idempotence.
A stale product edit keeps the unsaved draft visible, disables Save revision, and offers Reload shared.
Two disconnected exact-parent product-controller edits survive as siblings and converge to the same deterministic current turn on both peers.
Malformed scenario history disables manual writes before a new turn revision is added.
The product renders no more than 50 conversation turns per page and no more than the 50 most recent lineage revisions per turn.
The product states that installation-provided researcher identity and local time are not authenticated.
The editable turn workspace is injected into the existing live-Y.Doc scenario workspace; no parallel turn store was introduced.
notProved: Two packaged physical installations edited the same turn through a real Drive workspace and displayed sibling lineage after reconnect.
Authenticated participant identity, trusted timestamps, moderation, or explicit sibling-branch reconciliation beyond deterministic projection.
Packaged pointer, keyboard, focus, screen-reader, narrow-layout, reduced-motion, and every-theme interaction.
Near-limit turn counts, 500,000-character bodies, or 10,000-revision histories meet a measured latency and memory budget.
A release/updater artifact contains this development checkpoint.
